subject: physics
title: Scalars, vectors and resolving
key_idea: A scalar has size only. A vector has size and direction. Vectors are added tip to tail, and any vector can be split into two perpendicular components, F cos θ and F sin θ, that act independently.

blocks.text: Physical quantities are either scalars or vectors. This section covers the difference and how vectors are written.

items.meaning: A quantity with both magnitude and direction.

items: A vector is written in bold (**F**) or with an arrow over the letter.
Its magnitude is written without the bold or arrow, for example F.
A vector is drawn as an arrow. Its length shows the magnitude and the arrowhead shows the direction.
A negative vector has the same magnitude but the opposite direction.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Sort each quantity into scalar or vector.
diagram.prompt: Is each quantity a scalar or a vector?

items: Scalars have size only. Vectors have size and direction.
Distance, speed and mass are scalars. Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force are vectors.

blocks.text: Vectors cannot be added as plain numbers. This section covers how to find the resultant of two coplanar vectors, which lie in the same plane.

items.meaning: The single vector that has the same effect as the vectors added together.

items.text: Choose a scale, such as 1 cm for 10 N.
Draw the first vector as an arrow with the correct length and direction.
Draw the second vector starting from the tip of the first.
Join the tail of the first to the tip of the second. This is the resultant.
Measure its length and convert with the scale. Measure its angle with a protractor.

blocks.text: Two vectors at right angles form a right-angled triangle, with the resultant as the hypotenuse.

blocks.label: Magnitude of the resultant
where: A, B = magnitudes of the two perpendicular vectors (same unit)

blocks.label: Direction of the resultant
where: θ = angle between the resultant and vector A (degrees)
B = the vector opposite θ, A = the vector next to θ

items: To subtract a vector, add its negative: **A** − **B** = **A** + (−**B**).
Reverse the arrow of **B**, then add tip to tail as before.
Vectors in a straight line add by plain addition, using + and − for the two directions.

diagram.alt: A practice calculation. Find the magnitude of the resultant of two perpendicular forces.
diagram.question: Two forces of {a} N and {b} N act at right angles to each other on an object. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force.

items: Add vectors tip to tail. The resultant joins the start to the end.
At right angles use R = √(A² + B²) and tan θ = B / A.
Subtract a vector by adding its negative.

blocks.text: A vector can be split into two perpendicular components. Each component acts independently of the other.

items.meaning: The effect of a vector in one direction. Two components at right angles can replace the original vector.
Splitting a vector into two perpendicular components.

blocks.label: Component along the direction at angle θ
where: Fx = component next to the angle θ (N)
θ = angle between the vector and the x direction (degrees)

blocks.label: Component perpendicular to that direction
where: Fy = component opposite the angle θ (N)
θ = angle between the vector and the x direction (degrees)

items: Draw the vector as the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.
Cos goes with the side next to the angle. Sin goes with the side opposite it.
The two components can be used in place of the vector, for example one along a line and one perpendicular to it.
Always check which angle is given before choosing sin or cos.
On a slope at angle θ to the horizontal, the weight W acts vertically downwards.
The component of weight along the slope is W sin θ.
The component of weight perpendicular to the slope is W cos θ.
The component along the slope pulls the object down it. The perpendicular component presses it into the surface.

items.text: A 20 N force acts at 30° above the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components.

items: Fx = F cos θ and Fy = F sin θ for the components next to and opposite the angle.
On a slope, weight resolves into W sin θ along it and W cos θ perpendicular to it.

checks.q: State the difference between a scalar and a vector, and give one example of each.
checks.a: A scalar has magnitude only (for example speed or mass). A vector has magnitude and direction (for example velocity or force).

checks.q: Two forces of 6.0 N and 8.0 N act at right angles on an object. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force.
A box of weight 50 N rests on a slope at 20° to the horizontal. Calculate the component of the weight along the slope.
checks.a: Component = W sin θ = 50 × sin 20° = 17 N.

blocks.text: Calculations add two vectors at right angles. Scale drawings may use vectors at any angle.

items: Examples of scalars and vectors include velocity and speed, mass, force and weight, acceleration, displacement and distance.
Problems can be solved either by resolving the forces or by drawing a closed triangle of forces.
A body is in **equilibrium** when it is at rest or moving at constant velocity. The resultant force is then zero.
Two forces in equilibrium must be equal and opposite.
Three coplanar forces acting at a point are in equilibrium when their vectors form a closed triangle, tip to tail.
Know examples of scalar and vector quantities and recognise vector notation.
Resolve a vector into two components at right angles by drawing and by calculation.
Find the resultant of two coplanar vectors at any angle by drawing, and at right angles by calculation.
Use a vector triangle to find the resultant of any two coplanar vectors, by calculation or by scale drawing.
Resolve a vector into two perpendicular components with Fx = F cos θ and Fy = F sin θ.
